Best for the refreshed 2025–2026 Model Y. Requires a separate projector and is for parked use only.

The supplied comparison also lists a Hansshow 18.5-inch flip-down overhead screen at $1,049 for compatible vehicles, excluding the Juniper Standard trim.

My recommendation

For kids watching shows on drives: Choose a dedicated rear display if your car is a 2020–2024 Model Y; otherwise, consider a tablet mount or a compatible screen for your exact trim.

For a refreshed 2025–2026 Model Y: Check whether your car already has Tesla's factory 8-inch rear touchscreen before spending hundreds on an upgrade.

For camping and parked movie nights: Buy the Aurzen TravelPlay screen and the standard ZIP projector. It's a relatively inexpensive, portable setup compared with a permanently installed overhead monitor.

One important distinction: the projector setup is intended for use while parked, whereas a rear touchscreen or tablet can be used by passengers on the road.
